reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it profiles a small-business support program offering education, services, and access to capital. Participants discuss their business experiences, leadership learning, and reported growth, while workplace visuals support that theme. Access to capital is described as part of the program, not as a request for viewers to transfer money or provide credentials; the program’s claims and outcomes remain unverified.

citations.quote: an initiative which aims to help create jobs and economic growth by providing small business owners with practical business education, business support services and access to capital.
After our orientation I was in tears because I finally felt like I was in the room with people who knew what they were doing and were serious about it.

If you look at those participants that went through the Goldman Sachs 10,000 small businesses program they've increased jobs they've also seen a lot of their profits increase at a higher rate than the national and regional economy as well.
I learned from the program that I was able to create the vision and then have our employees execute the vision.
After the program we closed out and we had 25% growth.

opening.argument: The video connects participation in a branded program with promised economic benefits. One participant describes an “opportunity to participate,” while the program is presented as providing access to capital and the testimonials associate participation with increased jobs, higher profits, and 25% growth. That combination functions as a recruitment-oriented promise: take part in the program and gain business growth. The precise action is framed as participation rather than a direct payment, but the requested commitment and the advertised financial upside are still linked.

citations.quote: when I saw the opportunity to participate with this 10,000 small businesses
providing small business owners with practical business education, business support services and access to capital.
they've increased jobs they've also seen a lot of their profits increase
After the program we closed out and we had 25% growth.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense says there is no request to transfer money or provide credentials, but that does not answer the more relevant concern: the video promotes participation by pairing it with capital access and unusually favorable growth testimonials. Calling the action “participation” does not make the implied benefit less promotional, especially when the program is presented as producing 25% growth.

citations.quote: access to capital
After the program we closed out and we had 25% growth.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted material does not show that viewers are promised a free reward or payment for taking a simple action. It describes a business-support initiative and participants’ experiences, while the reported growth concerns businesses that already went through the program. Nothing in these quotes establishes a viewer-facing claim, enrollment mechanism, or guaranteed return.

citations.quote: an initiative which aims to help create jobs and economic growth
those participants that went through the Goldman Sachs 10,000 small businesses program
The growth that I initially projected while in the program was about a 5% year-over- year for the next five years

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: a named financial institution, repeated testimonials, access to capital, and a specific 25% growth result. The video does not merely discuss business education; it repeatedly says the program “really works,” reports profits and job growth, and presents participants as evidence. The combination can make a favorable outcome seem readily attainable through association with the program, while the testimonial format supplies persuasion in place of independently demonstrated results.

citations.quote: One thing about the Goldman Sachs 10,000 Small Business Program is that it really works.
After the program we closed out and we had 25% growth.
they've increased jobs they've also seen a lot of their profits increase
access to capital

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls the outcomes unverified, but that is precisely the concern: the video prominently supplies favorable testimonials without showing how those results were measured or whether they are typical. “It really works,” profit growth, and 25% growth create a persuasive impression that the cited institutional setting does not independently substantiate.

citations.quote: One thing about the Goldman Sachs 10,000 Small Business Program is that it really works.
they've increased jobs they've also seen a lot of their profits increase

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The presence of testimonials and a stated growth figure does not itself establish a scam mechanism. The material presents the 25% figure as one participant’s business result and describes the initiative as aiming to create jobs and economic growth, not as guaranteeing viewers a return. The evidence also does not show that participation is easy, free, or tied to a cash payout.

citations.quote: After the program we closed out and we had 25% growth.
an initiative which aims to help create jobs and economic growth
If you look at those participants that went through the Goldman Sachs 10,000 small businesses program

opening.argument: Although the video uses interviews and workplace footage, its role is promotional: the title identifies Goldman Sachs and the program, the description highlights capital access, and the speakers repeatedly praise the program’s impact and results. The footage of operating businesses and the closing “WE CREATE” presentation reinforce an aspirational message rather than supplying neutral scrutiny. By framing participation as the route to stronger leadership, profits, jobs, and growth, the video steers viewers toward the program while appearing educational.

citations.quote: 10,000 Small Businesses in Southern California: Goldman Sachs
business support services and access to capital.
The Goldman Sachs 10,000 Small Businesses program has had tremendous impact.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense describes interviews and workplace visuals, but those elements can make promotion more credible rather than make it neutral. The title foregrounds the corporate sponsor, while the narration repeatedly praises the program and its results. The absence of a direct money-transfer request does not negate a promotional enrollment message built around promised business improvement.

citations.quote: 10,000 Small Businesses in Southern California: Goldman Sachs
The Goldman Sachs 10,000 Small Businesses program has had tremendous impact.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A promotional tone is not enough to establish a scam. The cited title and description identify the subject and describe education, support services, and capital access; they do not show a deceptive claim, payment demand, or guaranteed outcome. The workplace footage and participant interviews are consistent with documenting business education and operations, even if the presentation is favorable.
